question: ______ river forms boundary between the two States of Telangana and Maharashtra.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pranahita.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pranahita river** forms boundary between the two States of **Telangana and Maharashtra. **
 
• The Pranhita River is the largest tributary of the Godavari River, occupying 34% of its drainage basin, which carries the combined waters of the Penganga River, the Wardha River, and the Wainganga River. 
 
• The river flows through the entire** Vidarbha region in Maharashtra, as well as the southern slopes of the Satpura range. **
 
• The Pranhita sub-basin is the seventh-largest in India, 109,078 km2 in size, rendering it larger than the individual basins of major rivers such as the Narmada River and the Kaveri River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Narmada** is a major west-flowing river in the Peninsular region.

 
 
• The Narmada rises in the Maikala range__ in the Eastern Madhya Pradesh region.
 
• Amarkantak is the place from where the Narmada river originates.
 
• The Narmada, along with the Tapi river, flows through the faults in the Vindhya and Satpura range, instead of the valley.
 
• The Narmada enters the Gulf of Khambat, just below Baruch.
 
 
 
• The **Kaveri river **basin falls in how** 3 states and a union territory **of India.
 
 
• It falls in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Kerala.
 
• It originates in the foothills of the Western Ghats at Talakaveri.
 
• Shimshal, the Hemavati, the Arkavati, Kabini, Bhavani River, Lokapavani, the Noyyal, and the Amaravati River. are some of the tributaries of the Kaveri river.
 
 
 
• The Brahmaputra originates from the Chemayundung glacier near Manasarover lake in Tibet.
 
 
• In Bangladesh, Brahmaputra is known by the name Jamuna.
 
• The Yarlung Tsangpo is the Tibetan name for the upper course of Brahmaputra.
 
• In Arunachal Pradesh, Brahmaputra is known by the name Dihang.
 
• Most of its course lies outside India.
 
• It flows through countries such as India, China, and Bangladesh.
 
• The Brahmaputra is also called the "Red River".
